primary_source_lessons.zisk_binary: The pinned binary AIR decomposes64-bit operands/results into bytes and delegates byte operations to a typed table. It adds helpers to reduce lookup expression degree and reconstructs operation-bus words. Its broad combined binary table has millions of rows; copying it is not a cheap replacement for our already-small dedicated byte AND/SHIFT tables.
primary_source_lessons.zisk_arith: Pinned arithmetic uses16-bit limbs, signed carries, and explicit division-zero/overflow logic. This demonstrates separation of ordinary arithmetic but does not justify reusing its integer bounds in M31:65535² exceeds p, and an eight-term convolution can reach about2^35. ADD16 input+input+carry stays below2^17 and is safe; multiplication needs split products or a separately proved carry argument.
primary_source_lessons.zisk_main: Main consumes/proves delegated operation and continuation buses. A narrower arithmetic chip alone does not remove CPU retirement rows or state/control authority; immutable fact-table multiplicities can reduce delegated rows only after a constrained caller bus routes the same operation tuple.
primary_source_lessons.airbender_tables: Pinned tables use byte AND/XOR/OR, two-byte range checks and16-bit ranges. The16-bit shift implementation has a22-bit key (16input,5shift,1direction), hence2^22 rows. This requires a complete table-domain cost, not merely counting fewer caller queries.
primary_source_lessons.airbender_subarguments: The pinned design precommits memory-related columns before common challenges and checks the same transcript during recursive verification. Its read-range induction requires unique canonical initialization, strictly increasing clocks and canonical writes; this is not permission to drop our already-qualified canonical-v3 obligations.
